blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Diffusion language models (DLMs) generate text through iterative denoising, enabling bidirectional context modeling and parallel token refinement. Recent studies have applied reinforcement learning (RL) to DLMs and improved their reasoning performance. However, the iterative denoising process makes credit assignment more challenging, as final outcome rewards provide limited information about how different tokens contribute to the final output. In this paper, we propose Denoising Token Credit Assignment (DTCA), a framework for token-level credit assignment in reinforcement learning for diffusion language models. DTCA estimates token contributions by measuring the improvement in prediction confidence of remaining masked positions after token commitment and groups these signals according to part-of-speech (POS) categories. These contribution weights are used to select informative denoising timesteps and assign token-level learning signals during RL training. DTCA further calibrates these learning signals according to token-level entropy changes induced by policy updates. Experiments on LLaDA-8B-Instruct show that DTCA consistently improves mathematical reasoning performance across different generation budgets, with gains of up to 9.0 points on MATH500 and 5.3 points on GSM8K over the base model.

blocks.en: 2 Introduction
blocks.zh: 2 导言

blocks.en:
Diffusion language models (DLMs) have recently attracted increasing attention as an emerging paradigm for language modeling due to their ability to model bidirectional context and perform parallel token refinement ( Labs et al., 2025 ; Google DeepMind, 2025 ; Song et al., 2025 ) , offering an alternative to autoregressive generation ( Nie et al., 2025 ; Sahoo et al., 2024 ; Ye et al., 2025a ; Yu et al., 2025 ) . Recent studies have explored reinforcement learning for DLMs by leveraging the generation process, mainly constructing learning signals from denoising trajectories or intermediate states during training ( He et al., 2026 ; Wang et al., 2025b ; Oba et al., 2026 ; Monsefi et al., 2026 ; Huang et al., 2025 ) . However, DLMs generate sequences through multiple denoising steps, where tokens are gradually committed and each commitment can affect the refinement of
remaining masked positions ( Ou et al., 2025 ) . Therefore, RL optimization in DLMs requires finer-grained credit assignment that considers how different tokens affect subsequent refinement.

blocks.en:
Achieving finer grained credit assignment requires estimating the contribution
of individual tokens during DLM denoising. Specifically, we measure token
contribution by how much a committed token improves the model’s prediction
confidence on the remaining masked positions. However, directly estimating such
token-level confidence improvements during RL training is challenging because
multiple tokens are committed at the same denoising step and interact through
the shared denoising process, making their individual effects difficult to
isolate. Moreover, the estimated contribution can vary substantially across
different rollout samples. To obtain more reliable estimates, we categorize
tokens by part-of-speech (POS) categories and aggregate their refinement
effects within each category. POS categories provide a natural grouping criterion because they capture
different linguistic functions, with nouns and verbs typically carrying lexical
information while determiners and adpositions mainly providing grammatical
structure ( de Marneffe et al., 2021 ) .

blocks.en:
The denoising behaviors of different POS categories are further analyzed using
rollouts generated from the GSM8K ( Cobbe et al., 2021 ) dataset. As shown in Figure 1 (a), different POS categories exhibit distinct commitment trajectories across denoising steps. NOUN maintains a relatively high commitment ratio, whereas VERB has a high ratio at the beginning that declines substantially over the denoising process. Other categories, such as ADP, DET, and ADJ, exhibit relatively lower commitment ratios with more stable variations. Figure 1 (b) further shows the confidence gain associated with different POS categories. Clear differences emerge across categories: VERB achieves the largest confidence gain, followed by NOUN and PROPN, whereas categories such as DET and ADP show relatively smaller gains. These observations indicate that POS
categories capture different denoising behaviors and refinement effects, making
them a useful basis for grouping tokens and estimating contribution weights.

blocks.en: Based on these observations, we propose Denoising Token Credit Assignment (DTCA) , a token-level credit assignment framework for reinforcement learning in diffusion language models. DTCA estimates token contributions from denoising refinement signals and aggregates them into POS-level contribution weights to obtain more stable and interpretable learning signals. These contribution signals are then used to select informative denoising timesteps and derive token-level learning signals during RL optimization. DTCA further incorporates an entropy-based credit calibration module inspired by OPEFO ( Xu et al., 2026 ) to calibrate the learning signals according to token-level entropy changes induced by policy updates. Experiments on LLaDA-8B-Instruct show that DTCA consistently improves mathematical reasoning performance across different generation budgets, with improvements of up to 9.0 percentage points on MATH500 ( Lightman et al., 2024 ) and 5.3 percentage points on GSM8K ( Cobbe et al., 2021 ) over the base model.

diffusion language models and use POS categories to estimate the effect of

mathematical reasoning benchmarks and validate the benefits of its key
components.

blocks.en:

blocks.en:
Removing Contribution Credit results in similar reward trajectories to DTCA,
but leads to substantially different update behaviors. In particular, the
variant with uniform credit assignment consistently exhibits larger gradient
norms throughout training while achieving comparable reward improvements. This
suggests that contribution-based credit assignment mainly affects the quality
of token-level learning signals, allowing the model to optimize with different
update dynamics rather than simply changing the final reward trend. By
considering token-level contribution differences, DTCA provides a more
structured learning signal than uniform credit assignment.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
We presented Denoising Token Credit Assignment (DTCA) , a framework for
fine-grained token-level credit assignment in reinforcement learning for
diffusion language models. DTCA estimates token contributions from the
confidence improvement of remaining masked positions after token commitment,
aggregates these signals by POS categories, and uses the resulting contribution
weights for denoising timestep selection and token-level credit assignment.
DTCA further calibrates contribution credits according to entropy changes
induced by policy updates, balancing entropy-increasing and entropy-decreasing
updates. On LLaDA-8B-Instruct, DTCA improves the reproduced base model by 6.8
percentage points on MATH500 and 2.1 points on GSM8K under the 256-step
evaluation setting. Training dynamics and component ablations show that
contribution-based credit assignment improves token-level learning signals,
while entropy-based calibration helps maintain more stable policy updates.
These results demonstrate that denoising dynamics provide useful information
for fine-grained credit assignment in reinforcement learning for diffusion
language models.

blocks.en: A.1 Diffusion Language Models
blocks.zh: A.1 传播语言模型

blocks.en:
Building on the denoising paradigm of diffusion models ( Ho et al., 2020 ) , diffusion language models (DLMs) generate text through iterative denoising ( Hoogeboom et al., 2021 ; Dieleman et al., 2022 ; Gulrajani and Hashimoto, 2023 ) rather than autoregressive next-token prediction ( Lou et al., 2024 ; Li et al., 2022 ; Ye et al., 2024 ) .
Early discrete diffusion language models explore masked generation objectives and iterative refinement for language modeling ( Austin et al., 2021 ; Sahoo et al., 2024 ; Shi et al., 2024 ) .
LLaDA scales this paradigm to large language models with a masked diffusion objective and demonstrates competitive language generation performance ( Nie et al., 2025 ) .
Subsequent works further study improved training objectives, generation strategies ( Wu et al., 2026a ; Xie et al., 2025 ) , scaling behaviors ( Ye et al., 2025b ; Gong et al., 2026 ; Wu et al., 2026b ) , and data efficiency under limited-data and multi-epoch training settings ( Prabhudesai et al., 2025 ; Ni et al., 2025 ; Gao et al., 2025 ) .
When applying reinforcement learning to these models, their iterative generation process requires particular consideration.
Unlike autoregressive models, DLMs maintain multiple intermediate denoising states, where tokens are progressively committed and remaining masked positions are refined.
This generation process introduces new challenges and opportunities for reinforcement learning in diffusion models.

LLaDA将这一范式规模化为带有蒙蔽传播目标的大型语言模型,并展示出具有竞争力的语言生成性能(Nie等人,2025年).

blocks.en: A.2 Reinforcement Learning for Diffusion Language Models
blocks.zh: A.2 加强传播语言模式的学习

blocks.en:
Reinforcement learning for diffusion language models requires optimization
methods that account for the iterative denoising process ( Raajesh et al., 2026 ; He et al., 2025 ) . Existing approaches
mainly adapt RL objectives ( Schulman et al., 2017 ; Shao et al., 2024 ; Zekri and Boulle, 2025 ; Ni et al., 2026 ) or exploit intermediate denoising information ( Xie et al., 2026 ) to
construct effective learning signals ( Tang et al., 2026 ; Rojas et al., 2026 ; Zhu et al., 2026 ) . d1 introduces diffu-GRPO ( Zhao et al., 2025 ) , Coupled-GRPO reduces likelihood
estimation variance through complementary masks ( Gong et al., 2026 ) , and ESPO
uses evidence lower bound as a proxy for sequence likelihood during RL
optimization ( Ou et al., 2026 ) . Other methods leverage denoising trajectories ( Yang et al., 2025 ) and
intermediate states to improve RL training, including TraceRL, RLDF, and
DiSPO ( Wang et al., 2025b ; He et al., 2026 ; Oba et al., 2026 ) . These methods demonstrate how diffusion
generation characteristics can be incorporated into RL optimization ( Zhao et al., 2026 ) . However,
they mainly focus on optimization objectives ( Zhong et al., 2026 ; Jiang et al., 2026 ) , likelihood estimation ( Wang et al., 2026 ) , or
denoising trajectories, while how to assign fine-grained credit to individual
tokens during the denoising process remains underexplored.

blocks.en: A.3 Fine-grained Credit Assignment
blocks.zh: A.3 优惠信贷转让

blocks.en:
Sequence-level rewards in language model reinforcement learning ( Ouyang et al., 2022 ; Guo et al., 2025 ) provide limited
information about which tokens or reasoning steps contribute to the final
outcome, motivating recent studies on fine-grained credit assignment ( Wang et al., 2025a ; Cheng et al., 2026 ) . Existing
approaches improve reward granularity through process supervision ( Uesato et al., 2022 ) , step-level
feedback, and token-level reward redistribution ( Tan et al., 2026 ) or importance estimation ( Lightman et al., 2024 ; Wang et al., 2024 ; Li et al., 2025 ; Cui et al., 2025 ; Kazemnejad et al., 2025 ; Li et al., 2026 ; Zhang et al., 2026 ) .
However, these methods are mainly developed for autoregressive language models,
where tokens are generated sequentially. For diffusion language models,
DACA-GRPO provides an initial exploration of token-level credit assignment by
weighting committed tokens according to denoising progress and changes in the
predicted probabilities of remaining masked positions ( Monsefi et al., 2026 ) .
Different from DACA-GRPO, DTCA estimates token contributions from confidence
improvements after token commitment, aggregates these signals according to POS
categories, and uses the resulting contribution structure for denoising
timestep selection and token-level credit assignment.

blocks.en: Appendix E Limitations
blocks.zh: 附录E 限制

blocks.en:
While DTCA provides an effective approach for fine-grained credit assignment in
diffusion language model reinforcement learning, several aspects remain open
for future exploration. DTCA uses POS categories to aggregate token-level
confidence improvements and obtain stable contribution estimates. This design
relies on the quality of POS alignment and annotation, and more accurate
token-level labeling strategies may further improve the estimation process.
Moreover, DTCA currently defines token contribution based on the confidence
improvement of remaining masked positions after token commitment. Developing
more principled theoretical formulations for contribution estimation in
diffusion language models remains an interesting direction. Finally, our
experiments focus on mathematical reasoning with LLaDA-8B-Instruct. Applying
DTCA to other tasks, such as code generation, may require adapting the token
grouping strategy to different token distributions and generation patterns.
Further evaluation on diverse diffusion language model architectures is also
needed to understand the general applicability of DTCA.
